Place a unit with a Death effect. Cast my damage spell on it: it dies, its Death effect fires. The spell becomes a trigger; needs my own unit in play.
Place a unit whose Death effect puts tokens. A sacrifice card kills it for supply; tokens fill the front cells it left, so the enemy faces new blockers.
column5: faeria: Death Walker + Rakoan Shield Mates

column4: I let my own unit die for supply or strength; the leave trigger fires on the exit and may bring it back changed.
Enemy unit in the facing front cell is returned to its hand, so my dot is free; the return triggers my unit to strike or grow, and the enemy pays supply to place it again.
Revive puts a dead unit back so its Place effect fires; the link is only the generic revive, the leave card does not change it.
My card sends the enemy's front unit back to hand; my unit that reacts to leaving hits or grows. Silence adds nothing here.
Sacrificing own units and gaining from kills do not feed each other; only the revive pair works, and that is another mechanic.
Moving enemy units and sacrificing own ones are unrelated; the one real pair is a returnhand loop.
column5: runeterra: Go Get It + The Old Timer

column4: Place a unit with Place text. Sacrifice it for supply. A revive-on-attack unit brings the dead one back, its Place fires again, and I sacrifice it once more.
Mostly generic links; only the repeat-Place card gives a real chain, and steal is not needed.
Place a unit whose Death effect puts tokens. Sacrifice it for supply: I get supply and tokens fill the cells it left, so the enemy front is still blocked.
column5: faeria: Death Walker + Rakoan Shield Mates

column4: Attack effects and moving enemies are independent; links are generic.
Small hits finish wounded enemies for kill-gain, but the pairs are generic.
Kill-gain and revive do not feed each other; the real pair is offering plus revive.
A damage spell can finish an enemy, but pairs are generic and the kill-gain unit is not set off by the spell.
Links are other cards' own texts; nothing feeds between a kill-gain and a steal.
My ping spell hits my own unit with a Death effect in my front row; it dies and its Death effect hits the enemy facing it. The enemy can only answer next turn.
column5: runeterra: Drop the Bomb + Phantom Prankster

column4: My push moves an enemy unit next to my stealer; the stealer is placed and takes the weak enemy beside it. The enemy cannot answer in between.
column5: duelyst: Teleport Enemy To Me + Synaptic Arbitrage

column4: Unit that takes an enemy unit on Place stands beside my other unit; a return card takes it back to hand, and I place it again to steal a second enemy.
My unit that makes tokens when placed is returned to hand and placed again; its Place puts new tokens in the front cells again.
My damage spell kills my own unit with a strong Place effect; a revive card brings it back from the discard pile and its Place acts again.
My unit dies and leaves a token on its cell; a revive card puts it back later and its Place effect puts tokens down again.
I place a token; Bloodletter hurts it and grows, so each token placed adds strength to the unit in my front row.
My steal spell counts as a spell: my unit on the grid grows from it while the spell takes a weak enemy unit from his front row.
